Title: What is LiveSync?
Content: LiveSync is a bridge which connects CLO and Unreal Editor (CLO LiveSync), or Marvelous Designer and Unreal Editor (MD LiveSync), and aims to shorten workflows requiring rendering in Unreal Engine. This is particularly useful if your workflow involves CLO or Marvelous Designer and Unreal Engine, however, it is worth noting that intermediate process of using other software products may be eventually eliminated as LiveSync continues to get updated. Traditional workflows involve repetitive yet tedious and destructive process of exporting garments as desired file formats and importing the results in Unreal Engine, since users need to manually manage properties expressing realistic garments in CLO or Marvelous Designer. This is caused by limitations of using specific file formats, and you can only imagine fatigue accumulated from doing file exports, imports, and potentially redoing everything if design for garments needs to be adjusted in CLO or Marvelous Designer. By establishing a direct bridge, CLO and Marvelous Designer can communicate with Unreal Editor, eliminating needs for file exports and imports. LiveSync features and workflows can be found in Using LiveSync via CLO/MD LiveSync Editor and MetaHuman workflow with LiveSync. LiveSync Tutorial

Title: Setting up Unreal Engine & LiveSync plugin
Content: Please note that installation process for CLO LiveSync and MD LiveSync is identical. Only the folder names of zip folders are different (CLO LiveSync vs. MD LiveSync). 1. Install Substance 3D for Unreal Engine plugin for a desired Unreal Engine version. 2. Unzip the downloaded zip folder (CLOLiveSync.zip or MDLiveSync.zip), then install LiveSync to UE 5.x by putting CLOLiveSync folder in the following directory of your Unreal Engine installation. (default directory path: C:Program FilesEpic GamesUE_5.xEnginePluginsMarketplace) This folder is where Substance 3D for Unreal Engine plugin is located. 3. Create a new project, or open an existing project. 4. Make sure that LiveSync and Substance 3D for Unreal Engine plugin are enabled in Plugins settings. 5. In the top toolbar, go to Edit - Project Settings, then locate Platforms - Windows options to find Targeted RHIs to set its value to DirectX 11. Please note that setting Targeted RHIs to DirectX 12 may cause unexpected graphics driver crashes in Unreal Engine 5 while using LiveSync. DirectX 11 and DirectX 12 can be used in following scenarios: DirectX 11: using Lumen and not using Path Tracer DirectX 12: disabling Enable Order Independent Translucency (OIT), and using Path Tracer rather than Lumen Experimental UE5 features often require DirectX 12. Please note that assets brought to Unreal Editor via LiveSync may not open if the setting bounces between DirectX 11 and DirectX 12. 6. In the top toolbar, go to Edit &gt Project Settings, and search transparency to locate Enable Order Independent Translucency (OIT) option to enable the option. 7. Restart Unreal Editor. 8. To launch Live Sync Editor, go to Window &gt CLO/MD LiveSync Editor.

Title: Creating Prop
Content: Objective Create Scene&ampProp items by using CLO and Marvelous Designer software. Required &amp Recommended Below are the requirements and recommendations when modeling a Prop. [Required] "Prop" refers to any prop mesh that goes into the Scene/Stage. The file should not include anything other than Prop meshes. (e.g. Select Prop Mesh only when exporting) The meshs normal direction must be facing outwards. In the Description, the following information about the product must be provided. (1) UV MAP unwrapping status O or X [Recommended] It is recommended to apply the same material to the part using the same material. UVs should be unwrapped so that they do not overlap so that customers can use a variety of textures. If mesh and the normal map have the same location and direction, it may cause overlapping and flickering issues during rendering. Be careful not to overlap the mesh. If the two vertices are overlapping, please weld them together. For the complex graphic pattern, please use the Normal map. (e.g., logo and pattern) It is recommended to use textures with a maximum size of 2048 pixels. The scanned OBJ is compatible, but the mesh should be re-meshed and editable. It is recommended to add a wire to express the sharp edge. Details 1. Converting ZSE format in CLO software: Only CLO-formatted files can be uploaded to CONNECT. In Scene&ampProp, the term 'Prop' refers to backgrounds and props, while 'Scene' encompasses the whole setup, including Props, Light settings, and Custom Views. All props are saved as ZSE format in CLO software. To save as ZSE format, you need to have OBJ files. If you have a different format other than OBJ, export as an OBJ format file from other 3D MODELING software. 1-1. Open CLO 1-2. Import OBJ as Scene&ampProp TYPE From the main menu, click FILE IMPORT OBJ Select a file and click OPEN Object Type Scene&ampProp Scale After setting the value as when you work with different tools, then click OK 2. How to modify Scene&ampProp format 2-1. Modify the materials of Prop Select the IMPORTED PROP file, and then you can change the material and properties of PROP in the Property Editor. Note : To easily rotate the PROP, right-click in the 3D viewer background Gizmo Select Local Coordinate. Press the number 4 or 6 on the keyboard to see the front side, click PROP and hold down the SHIFT and rotate vertically. 3. Ensuring the Prop is clearly visible from the front view in CLO and then saving it will guarantee good visibility in the viewer when the file is uploaded later. From the main menu, click FILE SAVE AS Scene&ampProp Select Auto or Custom thumbnail when saving. Select the location to save, and enter the product name to sell, and click SAVE. When saving in Scene&ampProp format, note that the set Light, Render, Custom View settings are also saved along with the file. 4. Title: Creating Pose
Content: Objective Create a Pose file (.pos) by using CLO and Marvelous Designer software. 1. How to Create a pose file (.pos) 1-1. Creating a Pose file (.pos) using an avatar file (.avt). 1-2. Creating a Pose File (.pos) using FBX, GLB, or GLTF. 1-1. Creating a Pose file (.pos) using an avatar file (.avt) To create a pose file (.pos) by manipulating the joints of an avatar (.avt), you must have an avatar file with joints already set up. 1. Launch CLO or Marvelous Designer. 2. From the main menu, click on File &gt Open &gt Avatar, or click on Avatar &gt Open in the Library. 3. In the 3D Window, go to Avatar Display &gt Show Avatar Joint (Shift + X) to switch to the avatar's joint mode. 4. Move the Avatar's joints to create your desired poses. 5. From the main menu, click on File &gt Save as &gt Pose. 6. After entering the name and path for a pose file (.pos), save it. Note: Pose files (.pos) generated with CLO or Marvelous Designer's official Avatars (FV2, MV2, KV1) are fully compatible with each other. 1-2. Creating a Pose file (.pos) using FBX, GLB, or GLTF. Create a pose file (.pos) using FBX, GLB, or GLTF files with Pre-defined pose settings. FBX, GLB, or GLTF file MUST contain the Avatar Mesh and Joints, with identical names and joint structures to the avatar file (.avt) that the pose file (.pos) will be applied. 1. Launch CLO or Marvelous Designer. 2. From the main menu, click on File &gt Import &gt FBX / GLB / GLTF. 3. Select and open the FBX, GLB, or GLTF file you want to utilize for the Pose file (.pos). 4. Manipulate the Avatar's Joint to create the desired pose. 5. From the main menu, click on File &gt Save As &gt Pose. 6. After entering the name and path for a pose file (.pos), save it. Note: The pose file (.pos) will not work properly if you are applying it to an avatar with a different joint structure. 2. NORMAL MAP, DISPLACEMENT MAP, OPACITY MAP, ROUGHNESS MAP, METALNESS MAP, BASE MAP (FUR) 1-2. If you are going to sell the actual products, enter the URL of the sales page. Entering the types of the selling products will help customers. 2-1. For fabric, you must enter the fiber content of the fabric. (Examples: Cotton100%, Cotton97%Spandex3%) (Examples) Write it without space. Cotton100% or Cotton97%Spandex3% 2-2. If you have registered Map on a fabric material, enter the information whether it is a solid or a pattern. (E.g., Solid, Pattern) (Examples) Solid or Pattern 3. Title: Creating Hair
Content: Objective Create ZACS content by using CLO software. (The 'Register Accessory' function, which registers accessory files (*.zacs), is only available in CLO and is not supported in Marvelous Designer.) 1. How to Create Hair to be registered as Accessory (ZACS) 1-1. Create Hair in other 3D software. 1-2. Create Hair with the patterns in CLO. 1-1. Create Hair in other 3D software. Below are the requirements and recommendations when modeling Hair. Required &amp Recommended [Required] The accessory file must be created in FBX / OBJ / COLLADA format to be registered as the ZACS. The meshs normal direction must be facing outwards. The file should not include anything other than Hair meshes. (e.g. select Hair Mesh only when exporting) Please specify the compatible avatars for the ZACS in the Description. [Recommended] It is strongly recommended to create hair mesh using a maximum of 200,000 triangles, and please make sure that the polygon count does not go over 200,000. If the mesh and the normal map share the same position and direction, it may lead to overlapping and flickering issues during rendering. Make sure to avoid overlapping the mesh. It is recommended to use textures using a maximum of 2048 pixels. It is recommended to create hair that does not exceed the shoulder line. (For long hair, it is essential to 'Deactivate Avatar.') Create a thumbnail image that shows the item well, which is recommended to be 400*300 pixels. To avoid abnormal collisions between garments and hair during simulation, creating a transparent Dummy Mesh that covers the entire hair is recommended. (Please refer to the Dummy Mesh Guide) Modifying content provided by other platforms may violate copyrights and result in the removal of the item. Before proceeding with hair production, you must prepare the avatar file for generating accessories (ZACS). If you already prepared an avatar to utilize for accessories (ZACS), you can skip this step. 1. Run CLO. 2. Open a custom Avatar AVT or CLO's avatar in the library. 3. Export the avatar as OBJ / FBX / GLTF or any format suitable for your 3D program. 4. Import the avatar file saved in step #3 into your 3D program and create a Hair Mesh. 5. Save the created Hair Mesh as FBX / OBJ / COLLADA. 1-2. Create Hair with the patterns in CLO. 1. Run CLO. 2. Open a custom Avatar AVT or CLO's avatar in the library. 3. However, the pattern to be converted must be created in advance before registering as an accessory. Note: After selecting the patterns to be converted into an accessory, you can register them as an accessory by right-clicking on the pattern in the 3D window, and then selecting Convert &gt to Avatar Accessory. Option Thumbnail [Auto/Custom] : Register the Thumbnail image for the ZACS to be created. When 'Auto' is selected, the Thumbnail image will be generated automatically. When 'Custom' is selected, click the '+' button to select the Thumbnail image you want to register. Save After choosing the save path for the ZACS, click the Save (S) button to generate the ZACS. 3. Modifying the material of ZACS You can modify the textures and materials applied to the generated ZACS in Property Editor. 1. Click on the ZACS in the 3D window. 2. Apply textures and materials in the Property Editor. 4. Saving the ZACS Save the Hair ZACS file with all textures and materials applied. 1. from the main menu, File &gt Save As &gt Accessory 2. After specifying the file name and directory path, click Save (S). 3. Save Accessory Select Accessory : Select the type of Accessories (ZACS) Use Custom Image : Register Thumbnail image. Title: Creating Zipper Sider&Puller
Content: Zipper Structure Slider &amp Puller Please check the requirements and recommendations for the Slider and puller below. [Required] The slider &amp puller(zipper) file format must be *.ZSS Slider &amp puller should be created in OBJ file format. The Slider &amp Puller OBJ file must consist of two or more meshes. When registering the zipper file, it will be all created in size #3 (100%). Please create the Slider &amp Puller file(OBJ) in size #3. The meshs normal direction must be facing outwards. Align the MESH position according to the purpose of each axis. (Same as the axis of the Slider) X-axis Place the point where the slider's zipper tape meets at the X-axis 0. Y-axis Sliders moving direction is on the Y-axis. The point where the zipper closes and where it touches should be placed at the Y-axis 0. Z-axis Place the slider's zipper tape face at the Z-axis 0. In the Description, the following product information must be provided. (1) Vertex Counts (2) UV MAP unwrapping status [Recommended] In the 'Select Mesh' section of the Register OBJ, please assign the name of the Slider Mesh as 'Slider' and the Puller Mesh as 'Puller' so that they are automatically recognized from the OBJ file. If the mesh and the normal map share the same position and direction, it may lead to overlapping and flickering issues during rendering. Make sure to avoid overlapping the mesh. If two or more vertices are located in the same place, please weld them together. For the complex graphic pattern, please use the Normal map. (e.g. logo, pattern, etc.) The scanned OBJ is compatible, but the mesh should be re-meshed and editable. It is recommended to add an edge loop(s) to define the sharp edge. &ltSlider &amp Puller Mesh's Position on the Grid&gt 1. Slider &amp Puller Registration Open CLO S/W Register OBJ from the Main Menu &gt Material &gt Zipper &gt Register OBJ Basic Type : Slider &amp Puller Name : Enter the name of the file to be created. Scale : Select the same scale unit when creating the OBJ. Axis Convention : Set up the axis so the Zipper can be positioned properly. File OBJ : Import the OBJ file to register as Slider &amp Puller Select Mesh : Select the mesh corresponding to Slider &amp Puller from the OBJ file. *If the Mesh names in the OBJ file are Slider/Puller, they can be automatically recognized as Slider &amp Puller. Preview : Check the imported Slider &amp Puller file in advance. Puller Position : Adjust the slider to place the right position where the puller is located on the slider. OK/Cancel : Click OK to finish the file creation when the file registration is done. The created file is saved in each object folder as Assets &gt Materials &gt Hardware_and_Trims &gt Zipper. 2. Title: Creating Avatar
Content: Objective Create an Avatar by using CLO and Marvelous Designer software. 1. Creating AVATAR Create an Avatar in other 3D software. Avatar files should be created in OBJ/FBX/GLB/GLTF formats, and avatars with joints are recommended to be in FBX formats. For avatars with textures applied, please make sure to check 'Embed Media' in the Export Option. Note: The following Skinning Methods are not compatible with CLO and Marvelous Designer: Dual Quaternion and Weight Blend. Required &amp Recommended Below are the requirements and recommendations when modeling Avatar. [Required] All mesh must be created in Y-axis(up) environment. You can import the following formats into Avatar Type: OBJ, FBX, GLB, and GLTF. All meshs normal direction must be facing outwards. [Recommended] For the best outfit-fitting performance, it is strongly recommended to create an avatar in either an A-pose or a T-pose. If mesh and the normal map have the same location and direction, it may cause overlapping and flickering issues during rendering. Be careful not to overlap the mesh. It is highly recommended to create and apply the avatar's various items, such as shoes, hair, earrings, etc., as separate assets instead of including them in the AVT file. The scanned data is compatible, but the mesh should be re-meshed and editable. The number of meshes can impact the speed of CLO, so it is strongly recommended to create an avatar using a maximum of 70,000 triangles. Unless you intended to model Avatar asymmetrically, we recommend creating Avatar's mesh and joint symmetrically. To fully utilize CLO / Marvelous Designer's Avatar IK feature, make sure that the joints' names and structure align with CLO/Marvelous Designer's Avatar. 2. IMPORT AVATAR Import the avatar files in the following formats into the Avatar Type: OBJ, DAE, FBX, GLTF Basic Load Type: Open Object type: Avatar Scale: Adjust the scale of Avatar. Object Camera: Check whether to import camera data or camera animation data. Joint Animation: Check whether to import animation data. Cache Animation(MC): Check whether to import Cache Animation (MC) data. Option Auto Add Arrangement Points: Automatically generate Arrangement Points and Bounding Volumes. Auto Create Fitting Suit: Automatically generate a Fitting Suit for the avatar. Note: It is strongly recommended to check 'Auto Add Arrangement Points' and 'Auto Create Fitting Suit' when importing. Move Garment to Start Position: Adjust the position of the garment to the starting point of the motions. Axis Conversion: adjust the axis of the Avatar. Translation Align Bottom to Ground: Adjust the position of the avatar to be placed on the ground. OK / Cancel Press 'OK' to import the Avatar, or press 'Cancel' to re-import the file to be used as the avatar. 3. Bounding Volume &amp Arrangement Points To dress the garment on the AVATAR, a process called 'Positioning' is needed. To carry out the 'Positioning' process, it is necessary to generate and modify the BOUNDING VOLUME and ARRANGEMENT POINT. Note: You can automatically generate both Bounding Volumes and Arrangement Points by selecting 'Auto Add Arrangement Points' during import. 3-1. Creating and Modifying Bounding Volume &amp Arrangement Points 1. from the Main Menu &gt AVATAR &gt AVATAR EDITOR 2. Click Arrangement Tab Please refer to the manuals below: Bounding Volume Arrangement Point 4. FITTING SUIT The 'Fitting Suit' is a fitting dummy generated by referring to avatars with various sizes and shapes, enabling automatic dressing by auto-grading garments onto the avatar. Note: You can automatically generate a fitting suit by selecting 'Auto Create Fitting Suit' during import. If the 'Fitting Suit' is not positioned correctly, please generate it manually. 4-1. Creating Fitting Suit 1. From the Main Menu &gt AVATAR &gt AVATAR EDITOR 2. Click FITTING SUIT Tab Please refer to the manuals below: Fitting Suit 5. Modifying AVATAR's Material If you want to modify the textures and materials applied to AVATAR, you can adjust them in the Property Editor. 1. Click the Avatar (AVT) in 3D Window 2. Apply the textures and materials in the Property Editor. 6. Save as AVT Save the AVT file with both textures and materials applied. 1. from the Main Menu, File &gt Save As &gt AVATAR 2. After specifying the file name and directory path, click Save (S). 7. If detailed information is missing, asset registration may be rejected during the item approval process. 1. Title: Creating 3D Garment
Content: Objective Create Garment content using CLO and Marvelous Designer software. Required &amp Recommended When creating and uploading a Garment file, please follow the rules below. [Required] The garment file format must be *zprj, *zpac. The garment should be simulated on your avatar (including hangers). The garment file may include an official CLO/Marvelous Designer avatar or an avatar with an authorized resale license when you upload an item in the Garment Category. The sewing lines should not be twisted. Collision issues between layers should be resolved if you are designing a layered garment. It is not possible to delete/add/replace the Trim and Fabric files after Publish. It is not possible to add, delete, or replace different Design Sources after Publish, for garments that include Design Sources. The majority of the components should consist of 2D patterns produced by pattern-making in CLO or Marvelous Designer software. The 2D pattern should have a reasonable particle distance. The recommended particle distance value is 5 to 20. 2D patterns should be arranged as neatly as possible in the center. Avoid overlapping patterns in the 2D Pattern window. 2D patterns that are the same pieces(e.g. Jackets, Pants, etc.) should be close to each other and should be easily recognized as one piece. The unnecessary notches and baselines inside the 2D pattern should be deleted before publishing. [Recommended] The garment should have Fitting Suit information for compatibility with the Auto Fitting function. The garment should be saved after deactivating the Strengthen, Freeze feature. You have to save the garment after simulating it in the A pose or the T pose. A collision between trims should be resolved if trim category items (e.g., Buttons, Zippers, Hardware, Fasteners, Notions) are added to the garment. Details 1. Loading Avatar - Use the default avatar from the software. Library Avatar - Use a customized Avatar from the software. Main Menu File Open Avatar Fitting Suit - CLO Software Users CLO's default avatar is wearing a Fitting Suit. Fitting Suit is a device that helps the CLO's Auto Grading function to work. If both avatars have Fitting Suit information when wearing the same 3D costume to different size avatars, they can be draped to the appropriate size for each avatar without any special pattern modification. If the outfit uploaded by the Seller is a ZPAC file using the CLO default avatar, the Auto Grading feature makes it easier for buyers to use 3D costumes. - Marvelous Designer Software Users The Marvelous Designer default avatar is also wearing a Fitting Suit. You can also add Fitting Suit information to your avatar if you are using the Marvelous Designer software version 10 or higher. Please refer to the link for detailed instructions. 2. Creating Patterns / Sewing / Simulation Create patterns using the pattern generation tool from the 2D window. Sew patterns created by using the sewing tool from the 3D or 2D window. When sewing is completed, press the simulation button to simulate the costume on the avatar. Particle distance For smooth operation speed, we recommend working at the default value of 20. When submitting the final costume file, make sure that the particle spacing is set as a reasonable value. By default, 5 is recommended, and 3 is recommended if the pattern is small. Layer When creating a costume with multiple layers, it must collide between layers. You can set the order of layers by setting the layer value from the simulation properties pane. It is recommended to change the value to zero after the simulation is complete. 3. Setting up textures From the Properties Editor, you can add/modify textures that are used for garments. 4. Saving Files Save the garment file according to the specified file format. - ZPAC Main Menu File Save as Garment If you save it through the above path, the only garment except the avatar is automatically saved. In this case, the file extension is saved as ZPAC. - ZPRJ Main Menu File Save as Project If you save it through the above path, the garment including the avatar is saved. In this case, the file extension is saved as .zprj. Note: Only ZPAC or ZPRJ files can be uploaded in the Garment category. 5. Content: Zipper Structure Slider Please check the requirements and recommendations for the Slider below. [Required] The slider(zipper) file format must be *ZSD or *ZSL. Please create the slider file(OBJ) in size #3. The meshs normal direction must be facing outwards. Align the MESH position according to the purpose of each axis. (If the position of the axis is not aligned, OBJ might not be created in the right place when creating a zipper.) X-axis Place the point where the zipper tape touches the slider at the X-axis 0. Y-axis Sliders moving direction is on the Y-axis. The point where the zipper closes and where it touches should be placed at the Y-axis 0. Z-axis Place the face of the zipper tape of a slider at the Z-axis 0. In the Description, the following product information must be provided. (1) Vertex Counts (2) UV MAP unwrapping status [Recommended] If the mesh and the normal map share the same position and direction, it may lead to overlapping and flickering issues during rendering. Make sure to avoid overlapping the mesh. If two or more vertices are located in the same place, please weld them together. For the complex graphic pattern, please use the Normal map. (e.g. logo, pattern, etc.) It is recommended to use textures with a maximum size of 1024 pixels. The scanned OBJ is compatible, but the mesh should be re-meshed and editable. It is recommended to add an edge loop(s) to define the sharp edge. you can't apply multiple materials to a slider but can render various materials using textures. Therefore, it's essential to have UV unwrapping done in a way that textures can be created without overlapping. &ltSlider Mesh's Position on the Grid&gt 1. Slider Registration 1. Open CLO S/W 2. Title: Garment Tab
Content: EveryWear Tutorial 1) Polygon Optimization Objective In the Garment Tab, adjust the Poly Count of the garment to match the platform you intend to export it to. Details You can manually input the desired Poly Count. It will display the current Polygon Count of the garment, including Trims. When the patterns mesh style is changed to Quad, it displays the total number of polygons, including the number of polygons changed to Quad and the remaining Triangles. You can also check the polygon counts in the bottom left corner of the 3D window. It will display the current Polygon Count of the garment, including Trims, converted into Triangles. It shows the Poly Count of the Avatar. Optimize the garment mesh according to the input provided in #1. If you enter a value smaller than the modifiable range, the value will be automatically adjusted and applied as the minimum value (variable). It switches to the Mask Brush tool. The EveryWear window temporarily closes, and the Brush tool appears in the upper-right corner of the 3D window. 1-1) Applying Mask Brush Objective Use the Mask Brush in the 3D and 2D windows to define the Mask area. Details Switch tabs to set the surfaces where the Mask will be applied. The Front and Back tab of the Mask Brush are based on the 2D pattern window, while in the 3D window, you can mask both sides. You can select a mode to either add or subtract from the mask area. Adjust the size of the Mask Brush. Clear all applied masks. Reset both Mode and Size. The Mask Brush window will close, and the EveryWear window will open. 2) Rigging Objective Rigging the garments to the avatar. Rigging is a fundamental aspect of 3D process, creating a skeleton structure with joints and bones to enable animations for 3D models. EveryWear's rigging merges the outfit with the avatar's joints, allowing them to move together. This rigging process also involves weight painting, which determines how much each part of the outfit is influenced by the movement of the avatars joints. This rigging process involves setting up and creating the controllable structure for the movement of the avatar and the outfit. CLO and Marvelous Designer specialize in detailed and realistic clothing animations through advanced garment simulations. However, for gaming purposes, the considerable data size of simulation-based clothing animations may not always be efficient. Therefore, EveryWear optimizes by utilizing Rigging instead of simulations to effectively synchronize the movements of outfits and avatars, prioritizing efficiency. Starting from version 2024.2 of CLO and Marvelous Designer, the accuracy of Auto-rigging has been further improved. Details Clothing is automatically rigged to the avatar. When rigging is applied, the Update and Brush tools will appear as shown in &ltImage2&gt If the avatar does not have joints or if there are multiple avatars within the same project, rigging will not proceed. When attempting to simulate the garment in the rigging state, the following warning message will be displayed. Yes : The rigging information will be deleted as soon as the costume is simulated, and the rigging menu returns to its initial state. No : The simulation will not proceed, and the existing rigging information will be maintained. Re-rig based on the current state of the garment. Navigate to the Brush tool. The EveryWear window momentarily closes, and the Brush tool appears in the upper right corner of the 3D window. Set the maximum number of joints that can affect each vertex. 3) Brush_Weight Objective Modify the weight value using the brush. Weight Painting ensures the rigged outfit moves seamlessly with the avatar's motions. Weight Painting adjusts joint influence on surrounding vertices for natural and fluid movements. While EveryWear auto-distributes weights based on the avatar, it's essential to check for any outfit penetration or inaccuracies in motion. Make necessary weight adjustments if needed. Details Set the Brush to Weight Mode. (Hotkey : Ctrl + ~) Change the blend mode. (Hotkey : Ctrl + Tab) Add : Add / Increase the weight value. Subtract : Subtract / Decreases the weight value. Smooth : Adjusts the weight value to match the surrounding areas. Set Brush properties. Strength : Adjust the intensity of the brush. (Hotkey : Alt + [ , ] ) Size : Change the size of the brush. (Hotkey : [ , ] ) Focal : Adjust the intensity difference between the center and edge of the brush. Depth : Set the depth of the brush's influence. Initialize the Brush property value. Exit the Brush tool and go to the EveryWear window. 3-1) Applying Weight Brush After selecting the Avatar's Joint, users can adjust Weight value by using a brush to add or subtract. Real-time Weight adjustments in 2D window are possible as well. Add Weight 1. Select Brush Tool: Press the Brush icon to open the Brush tool. 2. Choose Brush Mode: Set the Brush to Weight Mode. 3. Select Blend Mode: Configure the Blend Mode to Add. 4. Adjust Brush Properties: Modify the size and strength of the Brush according to your desired operation. 5. Choose Joint: While holding down Ctrl, click on the Joint. The selected Joint will be highlighted in yellow. 6. Apply Add Weight: Click and drag over the area you want to apply the brush. As the Weight value increases, it will be represented with a deeper red color. Subtract Weight 1.Select Brush Tool: Press the Brush icon to open the Brush tool. 2. Choose Brush Mode: Set the Brush to Weight Mode. 3. Select Blend Mode: Configure the Blend Mode to Subtract. 4. Adjust Brush Properties: Modify the size and strength of the Brush according to your desired operation. 5. Choose Joint: While holding down Ctrl, click on the Joint. The selected Joint will be highlighted in yellow. 6. Apply Subtract Weight: Click and drag over the area you want to apply the brush. As the Weight value decreases, it will be represented with a deeper blue color. When the Weight value is 0, no weight color information will be displayed. Smooth (Single Joint) This function smooths the Joint weight of vertices based on the selected joint, softly adjusting the weight differences with surrounding vertices. The sum of the joint weights for each vertex is always maintained at 1, and when the weight of the selected joint for a vertex is adjusted, the weights of the remaining joints are automatically scaled to maintain balance. However, if the weight of the selected joint is not different from that of surrounding vertices, no smoothing will occur. 1. Select Brush Tool: Press the Brush icon to open the Brush tool. 2. Choose Brush Mode: Set the Brush to Weight Mode. 3. Select Blend Mode: Configure the Blend Mode to Smooth (Single Joint). 4. Adjust Brush Properties: Modify the size and strength of the Brush according to your desired operation. 5. Choose Joint: While holding down Ctrl, click on the Joint. The selected Joint will be highlighted in yellow. 6. Apply Smooth Weight: Click and drag over the area you want to apply the brush. The Weight will be smoothly adjusted based on the surrounding values. Tips By applying the 'Full Smooth' function to the selected joint's skin weight, you can evenly smooth across the entire selected joint with one click, eliminating the need for manually painting weight with the Smooth brush. Usage: Click on the joint you want to modify to view its weight, then press Ctrl+Shift and click on the selected joint again. You can adjust the smoothing strength by modifying the 'strength' parameter under brush properties. Smooth (Multiple Joints) It operates for all joints, smoothing the joint weights of each vertex along with the weights of surrounding vertices. This is similar to selecting and using all joints in the Single Brush. In this process, the joint weights of each vertex are adjusted smoothly and simultaneously, while the sum of the joint weights for each vertex always remains 1. 1. Select Brush Tool: Press the Brush icon to open the Brush tool. 2. Choose Brush Mode: Set the Brush to Weight Mode. 3. Select Blend Mode: Configure the Blend Mode to Smooth (Multiple Joints). 4. Adjust Brush Properties: Modify the size and strength of the Brush according to your desired operation. 5. Apply Smooth Weight: Click and drag over the area you want to apply the brush. The Weight will be smoothly adjusted based on the surrounding values. Joint Lock The Joint Lock feature is designed to influence only specific areas when modifying weights in situations such as the following: When adjusting the weight value without affecting the selected joint. When unrelated joints are causing the weight issues and need corrections (e.g., armpits, corners, sleeves, skirts, etc.). When intricate weight adjustments are required for complex models. Locked Joints will remain unaffected when adjusting other joints weight values. 1. Select Brush Tool: Press the Brush icon to open the Brush tool. 2. Choose Brush Mode: Set the Brush to Weight Mode. 3. Lock the Joint: Hold down Alt and click on the Joint. The Locked Joint will be highlighted in red. To apply Lock to all joints, hold Alt and right-click on the desired joint. 4. Unlock the Joint: To unlock, Hold Alt and click on the locked Joint again. Once unlocked, the Joint will be displayed in white. To unlock all joints, hold Alt and right-click on the desired joint. Hammering Hammering is a feature that automatically adjusts the weight values of a specific vertex to closely match the surrounding weight values when there is a significant disparity. This feature comes in handy in situations where certain areas, like armpits, the bottom of pants, sleeves, and so on, are unintentionally affected by unwanted joints, resulting in awkward deformations or the strange spikes. 1. Select Brush Tool: Press the Brush icon to open the Brush tool. 2. Choose Brush Mode: Set the Brush to Weight Mode. 3. Select Joint: Hold down Ctrl and click on the joint. The selected joint will be highlighted in yellow. 4. Hammering: Hold down Shift and click on the desired vertex. When Shift is pressed, the mouse cursor changes from the brush shape to a red dot, indicating that it can recognize vertices. 4) Brush_Sculpt Objective Use the Brush to modify the shape of the garment. Details Set the Brush to Sculpt Mode. (Hotkey : Ctrl + ~) Change the blend mode. (Hotkey : Ctrl + Tab) Grab : Use this mode to grab and reshape the 3D clothing surface. Smooth : Use this mode to make the 3D clothing surface smoother. Fix Intersection : Use this mode to correct areas where intersections occur between the garment and the avatar or between the surfaces of the garment. Set Brush properties. Strength : Adjust the intensity of the brush. ( Hotkey : Ctrl + [ , ] ) Size : Change the size of the brush. ( Hotkey : [ , ] ) Focal : Adjust the difference between the brush center and edge intensity values. Depth : Set the depth of the brush's influence. Initialize the Brush property value. Exit the Brush tool and go to the EveryWear window. 4-1) Applying Sculpt Brush Using the Sculpt Brush allows users to modify the shape of the garment. Applying Grab Brush Utilize this brush when the garment penetrates inside the avatar or when garment layers overlap, causing visibility issues. 1. Select the Brush Tool: Open the Brush Tool by clicking on the Brush icon. 2. Choose Brush Mode: Set the Brush to Sculpt Mode. 3. Select Blend Mode: Set the Blend Mode to Grab. 4. Adjust Brush Properties: Modify the size and strength of the Brush according to your desired operation. 5. Apply Grab Brush: Click and drag over the area you want to apply the brush, and the selected area will move along with the mouse. Note that the Weight value will not have any effect. Applying Smooth Brush Utilize this brush to create a smoother surface for garments or to soften angular areas while modeling. 1. Select the Brush Tool: Open the Brush Tool by clicking on the Brush icon. 2. Choose Brush Mode: Set the Brush to Sculpt Mode. 3. Select Blend Mode: Set the Blend Mode to Smooth. 4. Adjust Brush Properties: Modify the size and strength of the Brush according to your desired operation. 5. Apply Smooth Brush: Click and drag over the area you want to apply the brush, and the surface will be smoothed based on its surroundings Applying Fix Intersection Brush Utilize this brush for areas where the garment intersects with the avatar or where garments overlap, as other existing brushes may struggle with these areas. 1. Select the Brush Tool: Open the Brush Tool by clicking on the Brush icon. 2. Choose Brush Mode: Set the Brush to Sculpt Mode. 3. Select Blend Mode: Set the Blend Mode to Fix Intersection. 4. Adjust Brush Properties: Modify the size and strength of the Brush according to your desired operation. 5. Apply Fix Intersection Brush : Apply the brush to the desired area to automatically correct intersections where the avatar or garments overlap.

Title: Creating Zipper Bottom Stopper
Content: Zipper Structure Bottom Stopper Please check the requirements and recommendations for the Bottom stopper below. [Required] The Bottom stopper(zipper) file format must be *ZSP or *ZST. When registering the zipper file, it will be all created in size #3 (100%). Please create the stopper file(OBJ) in size #3. The meshs normal direction must be facing outwards. Align the MESH position according to the purpose of each axis. X-axis Place the point where the zipper tape touches each stopper at the X-axis 0. Y-axis Top Stopper Position the point of the top stopper that aligns with the endpoint of the zipper tape at the Y-axis 0. Bottom Stopper Position the point of the bottom stopper that aligns with the bottom of the slider at the Y-axis 0. Z-axis Place the slider's zipper tape faces at the Z-axis 0. In the Description, the following product information must be provided. (1) Vertex Counts (2) UV MAP unwrapping status [Recommended] If the mesh and the normal map share the same position and direction, it may lead to overlapping and flickering issues during rendering. Make sure to avoid overlapping the mesh. If two or more vertices are located in the same place, please weld them together. For the complex graphic pattern, please use the Normal map. (e.g. logo, pattern, etc.) The scanned OBJ is compatible, but the mesh should be re-meshed and editable. It is recommended to add an edge loop(s) to define the sharp edge. Open Bottom Stopper From the Front View, the origin (0,0,0) is the bottom part where the slider can be all the way down. Therefore, place the stopper where it touches the slide at the origin. From the Top View, the zipper teeth are placed on the X-axis of 0. Place the zipper teeth of a stopper on the X-axis of 0. &ltThe position of each Open Bottom Stopper Mesh on the Grid&gt Closed Bottom Stopper From the Front View, the origin (0,0,0) is the bottom part where the slider can be all the way down. Therefore, place the stopper where it touches the slide at the origin. From the Top View, the zipper teeth are placed on the X-axis of 0. Title: Withdrawal of service
Content: Item revenue upon service withdrawal When you withdraw from the service, posting and selling of all items will be discontinued. If items previously sold by a seller who withdrew from the service are used as Design Source for new items and those new items are sold, the revenue will not be paid to the seller who withdrew from the service. When a seller withdraws from the service, the final revenue will be settled in the following month.

Title: Blocking items
Content: When Items are Blocked Items, either in whole or in part, may be blocked if they infringe on someone else's copyright. Items that are explicit or violent may be blocked. Items containing messages that are potentially controversial in areas such as politics or religion may be blocked. Items that cause discomfort to other users or receive continuous reports may be blocked. In cases where items are deemed incompatible with the policies of CONNECT, administrators may block them. Revenue when Paid Items are Blocked If a paid item is blocked, sales will be discontinued. Revenue from already sold items will be paid to the seller. If the reason for blocking the item is related to copyright, ownership of revenue from already sold items may be determined through legal procedures or discussions with the original creator. If a blocked item is used as a Design Source, generating revenue, the seller will not receive any revenue.

Title: Payout Schedule
Content: Payout in the following month Revenue from items sold between the 1st and last day of each month will be settled in the following month. Payout dates fall between the 15th and 30th of the following month, subject to variation due to holidays or maintenance. Wire Transfer Schedule Revenue from December to May will be paid out in June. Revenue from June to November will be paid in December. If an account has an issue on the payout day, it will be postponed to the next scheduled payout day. Refund Policy Refunds due to technical issues or payment cancellations will be deducted from the final revenue before the settlement date.

Title: Payout conditions
Content: To process settlement, ensure the following conditions are met: Seller's Information Verification Once seller's information is verified, the payout will be processed. Revenue accumulates before verification the payout is available once seller info is verified. When seller information is changed after initial verification, payout will be delayed for re-verification. Payout Available over USD $50 Access payout when total revenue, after fee deduction, exceeds USD $50. If revenue is under USD $50, expected payout accumulates. The payout is based on the sales revenue of $50 USD (taxes are not included). If you have US-resident buyers, their tax is deducted from the final payout. Note that the actual payout may vary after tax deductions. Payout Delayed Payout delays occur in the presence of copyright issues until resolution. Majority of buyer refund requests or submitted reports result in payout delay until it is solved. Payout will be temporarily disabled in cases of suspicious payments or payment system issues.

Title: Design Source Policy
Content: Create items using paid items (garments/trims/fabrics) You may sell created items by using paid items(garments/ trims/ fabrics). Garments can be purchased, modified, and sold as a second creation on CONNECT. However, trims and fabrics cannot be modified and re-sell. Trims can be only included in garments. Settlement when using paid items When created garments consist of paid items as a Design Source, the price of paid items will be added to your set price. When garments consisting of paid items are sold, the revenue of the Design Source will be distributed to the original creator. Revenue when your items are sold as Design Source When your items are sold and used as Design Source for other items, your items will be settled as your revenue. Examples Seller D created garments by purchasing Seller A's garment($10), Seller B's trim($2), Seller C's fabric($5). When Seller D sets the price of the garment, the total price will be automatically set as the sum of items A, B, and C, which is $17. When Seller D sets the margin as $20, the total price will be $37. When items are sold at $37, Seller D's revenue will be $20, Seller A's will be $10, Seller B's $2, Seller C's $5.

Title: Deduction amount & Payout amount
Content: The calculation of the seller's earnings is as follows. Total item sales amount (-) Design Source usage fee (-) Website deduction commission (-) Withholding tax Total item sales amount Total amount of items sold from the first to the last day of the month Includes items sold through Design Source when other sellers' items are sold (When someone resells my item as a component in a garment file, the price of my item is included in my sales revenue) (-) Design Source usage fee If paid items are used, the revenue is shared with the seller who created those items. (When a paid garment, fabric, or trims are purchased to create a paid garment, and the garment is sold, the price of the included paid items is categorized as the sales revenue of the seller of those items) (-) Website Commission Deduction 70% of the total sales amount is allocated as the seller's revenue, while 30% is deducted as a service fee. (-) Withholding tax For orders where the buyer is American, a withholding tax may be additionally applied. The withholding tax rate is calculated based on the agreed upon rate between the United States and the seller's country. [Example] Without using Design Source, a $100 item was created and sold, with the buyer not being from the United States, Total Sales Amount: $100 (-) Website Commission: $30 = Total Payment: $70 Using $10 fabric, a $100 item was created and sold, with the buyer not being from the United States, Total Sales Amount: $100 (-) Cost of Design Source Fabric: $10 (-) Website Commission: $27(30%) = Total Payment: $63 A Polish individual created a $100 item without using Design Source and sold it to a buyer from the United States, Total Sales Amount: $100 (-) Website Commission(30%): $30 = User's Earnings: $70 (-) Withholding Tax (5% between Poland and the United States): $3.5 = Total Payment: $66.5 A Korean individual created a $100 item using $30 buttons and sold it to a buyer from the United States, Total Sales Amount: $100 (-) Cost of Design Source Buttons: $30 (-) Website Commission(30%): $21 = User's Earnings: $49 (-) Withholding Tax (10% between South Korea and the United States): $4.9 = Total Payment: $44.1

Title: Seller Information Guide
Content: Find Seller Information Here 1) Select the profile image at the top right of the CONNECT page. 2) Select the Sales menu. 3) Select the INFO tab on the Sales page. Non US seller (Individual): For individuals who are not corporations, including those who are not American or Americans who do not reside in the USA. The information must be reviewed and approved by an administrator for the Seller Info registration to be finally completed. The review process can take from 1 to a maximum of 10 business days. During the Pending status, the information can be edited or updated. Rejected This status indicates that the Seller Info has not been finally approved and has been rejected. By clicking the message icon to the right of the REJECTED text, you can view the reasons for the rejection. You can modify the Seller Info and resubmit it by pressing the SUBMIT button again. Title: Item Inspection
Content: Objective Upload the item to CONNECT followed by the guidelines. Free and View Only items are posted at the same time as you click the Publish button. However, items that are already published may be rejected or blocked according to the guidelines. Note: 3D File Status If the item is blocked, the item will be deleted by the operator. If the item is rejected, you should modify the item according to the guidelines and publish it again. Details Please check the criteria of Reject and Block below and follow the guideline. Block Criteria Reject Criteria Block Criteria If you do not follow the guidelines below, the item may be deleted by the operator. Do not include content containing the Corporate Identity and Brand Identity of CLO or Marvelous Designer. Do not contain content from unauthorized brands. Do not copy products from specific brands. Do not include content that does not have a redistribution license. Do not include content purchased from similar sites. Do not include words and content that adversely affect society. Do not include content that promotes other marketplaces or digital stores or exposes social media accounts. Do not include content that can cause other problems. Reject Criteria Please upload the item by following the guidelines below. Items cannot be uploaded until they are modified. 1. Common All content in CONNECT must comply with the following criteria: The title of the item must be appropriate to the uploaded file. Tags, categories, and descriptions must be appropriate to the uploaded file. The thumbnail and additional images be appropriate to the uploaded file. The attached files should be appropriate to the uploaded file. If the item is also selling the physical product, you must enter the URL of the sales page (e.g. https://connect.clo-set.com/). 2. Item Guidelines The detailed guidelines for each item type in CONNECT are as follows. [Garment] The garment file format must be *zprj, *zpac. The garment should be simulated on your avatar (including hangers). The file should exclude avatars when you upload an item in Garment Category. The sewing lines should not be twisted. Collision issue between layers should be resolved, if you are designing a layered garment. It is not possible to delete/add/replace the Trim and Fabric files after Publish. It is not possible to delete/add/replace the original garment files after Publish, for garment using original garment files. The majority of the components should consist of 2D patterns produced by pattern making in CLO or Marvelous Designer software. The 2D pattern should have reasonable particle distance. The recommended particle distance value is 5 to 20. 2D patterns should be arranged as neatly as possible in the center. Avoid overlapping patterns in the 2D Pattern window. 2D patterns that are the same pieces(e.g. Jackets, Pants, etc.) should be close to each other and should be easily recognized as one piece. The unnecessary notches and baselines inside the 2D pattern should be deleted before Publish. [Fabric] The fabric file format must be *zfab. You must enter the weight and thickness of the fabric in the Description. You must enter information for the applied MAP. (TEXTURE, NORMAL MAP, DISPLACEMENT MAP, OPACITY MAP, ROUGHNESS MAP, METALNESS MAP, BASE MAP) You must enter the measurement information (whether the equipment is used, the name of the equipment, and the measurement institution) in the Description. You must enter the fiber content of the fabric in Tag. (e.g., Cotton 100%, Cotton 97%, Spandex 3%) You must create a file by used for the fabric material according to the repeated image. The size of the Maps used for fabric material must be 4K or less. [Trim] The trim file format must be *trm. The position and rotation of the mesh should be set as 0, and the size should be set to 1. When making an OBJ trim, the unit of the production environment should be set to mm. All mesh must be created in Y-axis (up) based environment. The meshs normal direction must be facing outwards. TRIM must be located at the origin (0,0,0). Mesh and Texture must match. In the Description, the following information of the product must be provided. (1) DEFAULT SIZE (X, Y, Z unit: mm) and WEIGHT (unit: g) of TRIM. (Refer to Property Editor in CLO) (2) UV MAP unwrapping status [Button] The button file format must be *btn. The position and rotation of the mesh should be set as 0, and the size should be set to 1. All mesh must be created in Y-axis (up) based environment. The meshs normal direction should be facing outwards. The point where the OBJ button will be anchored to the garment must be placed at the origin (0,0,0)). When making an OBJ button, the unit of the production environment should be set to mm. The top side of the button should be made in the positive Y-axis direction. Mesh and texture must be matched.
